lines: Word came up from the works. You went in the deep lane, then.
Half the city did not think Vane would even let you try.
The other half has never met Vane.
First time? You will get lost. Everybody gets lost. It is not a grid, it is a habit.
Straight on for the Tide Hall. Downhill for the water. The canal splits everything else.
If you can smell fish you have gone west. If you can hear hammers you have gone east.

tg_washer: Four hundred rooms on this row and I do the sheets for a hundred and twelve of them.
None of them were let to travellers this spring. All of them were let.
Whoever they are, they change their own beds and they do not want me in the room.
tg_kid_a: There is a light at the end of the west mole and I am not allowed to walk to it.
So I have counted it instead. Nine hundred and six paces, from the map.
I am going to walk it the day I am twelve and nobody can stop me.
tg_tenant: Rent went up in the spring and half the stair took Foundation work to cover it.
Nobody is angry. That is the strange part. Everyone is grateful.
It is hard to be suspicious of the people who pay for your dinner.
tg_oldhand: I have lived in this city seventy-one years and it has never had this many strangers in it.
Not a bad kind. A busy kind. Everyone with somewhere to be and a case in their hand.
Busy is what a city looks like just before something happens to it.
tg_lamplighter: Three hundred and forty lamps, from the north wall to the light on the mole.
I light them in an hour and ten. It was an hour and forty before the new oil.
Foundation gave us the oil. Free. They gave us everything, and it all works.

lines: Word came down off the north road this morning. The Hall is not saying anything.
We have doubled the lamps on the sea gate, mind. Nobody asked us to.
Three Crests, and he took the deep lane to get the third.
Mabry has not decided whether she is furious. She keeps saying "the deep lane" to herself.
The loud one was in the gallery for the speech. Front row. Did not heckle once.
I had money on him heckling.
The Tide Crest. In the works, in the water, off Marit Vane herself.
I have cried this square for six years and I have said that sentence nine times.
Go and get dry. Nobody wants a soaked hero dripping on the Basin.
THE TIDE HALL IS OPEN. KEEPER MARIT VANE SITS TODAY.
Challengers go DOWN, into the works. It is water down there and it is cold.
And do not swim in the Basin. It is a monument. It is not a bath.

tg_challenger: Fourth attempt. She has put me in the water four times and I have thanked her four times.
That is not sarcasm. She stops the moment it stops being a fight.
You will lose to Vane and you will not be frightened while you do it.
tg_hall_kid: Mum says the Basin is the sea in a box so the Hall can look at it.
I say it is a puddle they charged everyone for.
We have agreed not to talk about it any more.

lines: The loud one came in and asked whether we treat people. Not kin. People.
I said yes. He said good, and went out again. I did not care for that at all.
Three Crests in him now and he still turns up soaked to the collar.
I have started keeping a towel back with his name on it.
He sat in my waiting room for an hour after his kin were done. Just sat.
Then thanked me twice and left.
Not for me. For my brother. He works the east mole and something went over his foot.
Third one this month off that berth. They will not say what they are moving.
Everyone is very sorry and nobody will say what they are moving.

tg_glassblower: Tideglass. Not for the harbour, whatever the harbour board tell you. For us.
Sand off the bar and ash off the kelp and a furnace that has not gone out in ninety years.
Come in and watch. Everybody watches. It is why we put the window in.

lines: Everyone on this wharf has heard about the north road by now.
Your friend has not made one joke all morning. That is how I know it was bad.
Your friend took the Channel Crest off Mabry, and he went down the deep lane to do it.
Nobody goes down the deep lane on purpose. He came up laughing.
That loud friend of yours went to hear Dr. Veyl on the wharf and came away very quiet.
Said the man seemed decent and it was bothering him. Strange thing to complain about.
There's a lad been sat on the milestone since dawn with a slate, counting carts.
I asked him why. He said somebody had to, and offered me his tea.
TWO MEN TAKEN ON THE NORTH ROAD. HARBOUR WATCH ASK FOR WITNESSES.
That is all I have been given and I have been asked to leave it there.
I have cried this street eleven years. I have never been asked to leave it there.
DR. VEYL SPEAKS ON THE WHARF - THAT HAS BEEN AND GONE, YOU WERE THERE.
Everyone came away with the same face on. I have seen that face at weddings.
TIDE HALL OPEN. FISH AUCTION AT FOUR. NOBODY BUY THE SMALL CRAB.
DR. CASSIAN VEYL SPEAKS ON THE WHARF THIS AFTERNOON. ALL WELCOME.
STORM RESEARCH AND COASTAL SAFETY. FREE. NO COLLECTION.
That last part is why the whole city is going.
He bought every Dusk Vessel on the shelf and asked what else works after dark.
Sixteen years old, asking me that. In my shop.
Boy with three Crests came in dripping on my floor and bought rope.
Rope. In a Kin shop.
The green-jacket lad bought six storm cards and would not take them for nothing.
Said if they were free then somebody else was paying.
Best spring the Parade has had in twenty years, and not one copper of it is fish.
It is wages. Foundation wages, spent in my shop, on a Tuesday.
I would be a fool to ask where the money comes from and I have been a fool before.
Vane gave you the Crest. Then I will tell you what I told her, and she went quiet too.
Berths eleven to twenty took soundings off my harbour for six weeks. Always after dark.
A survey is a survey. But an honest one does not need the dark.
Tideglass. Four hundred boats, and a hundred and nine of them working.
Not for want of crew. For want of a channel worth putting a boat down.
Vane is in the works. She has been in the works since Tuesday.

tg_netter: The flats are heaving. Everything that lives deep has come up onto the mud.
My mother would have called that a gift year. It is not. It is a run.
Things run from something. Nobody down here finishes that sentence.
tg_fishwife: Ninety slabs under that roof and eleven of them working.
I have stood at mine since I was nine and I will stand at it empty.
Somebody has to be here when it comes back. That is a job too.
tg_child: Dad says the sea is holding its breath.
So I asked what happens when it lets go. He did not answer.
So I asked louder. He still did not answer.
tg_porter: Fish out of the market, crates onto the mole, and it is the same shoulder either way.
Crates pay four times what fish pays now. Four.
I am not complaining. I am telling you a number, because the number is the strange part.
tg_dockhand: Berths eleven to twenty are one charter and they run their own hands.
We are not allowed past the rope. In my own yard, that I have worked eleven years.
They are polite about it. Everyone is very polite about all of this.
tg_shipwright: Eleven boats built this year and not one of them can carry a fish.
Shallow draught, heavy fittings, big deck winch. That is a boat for lowering things.
Whatever they are lowering, they have been lowering it since the frost.

lines: Heard him, did you. Everybody heard him. He is very hard to argue with.
I have carried his gear down the ridge road twenty-two times this month.
I still could not tell you what any of it does, and I have started wanting to know.
Down the ridge road, four a day, and every one of them under a tarpaulin.
Off the dray, onto the mole, onto the water, gone before dark.
Twenty-two loads and not one of them stayed in Tideglass. Think about that.

tg_institute_hand: The Institute measures and the Foundation pays for the instruments. That is the arrangement.
It has been the arrangement for eleven years and it has been a good one.
This spring is the first time anybody upstairs has asked us to hold a result back.
tg_gaugeman: Come and look at the drum. Two hundred years of the same handsome wave.
Then look at the last four. Flat. Not low. Flat.
The sea does not go flat. The sea is the one thing that is never flat.

lines: You have met the Director's daughter, I hear. Then I do not have to perform.
Here is the part we leave out because it does not persuade anybody.
We do not know what happens to everything that migrates once the current stops.
We have models. They disagree with each other. Loudly.
Depth soundings. Standard work. Very dull.
No, I cannot give you the numbers. No, that is not sinister, it is a form.
...I would like it to be dull. I would like that a great deal.
You are welcome inside. You are always welcome inside. Please believe that.
I heard what happened on the north road and I have not slept since.
Nobody in this building would do that. I need that to be true, so I am saying it.
The Coastal Station is open to anyone. Gallery, gauges, the storm glass wall.
We put out the warning that brought nine crews home in the spring.
You will hear things about us. Come in first, then hear them.
The Tide Crest. Good. Keep going, and keep going away from here.
I have asked four questions this week and had four true answers.
That is what frightens me. Nobody is lying to me. They simply do not think it is wrong.
I have not gone home. I have written the letter four times and not sent it.
They were Foundation. Not hired, not strangers. Ours.
I am going to find out who sent them, and then I am going to be very difficult about it.

tg_lampkeeper: Nine hundred and six paces out and the same back, every night of my life.
The light does not care whether anyone is watching. That is the good of it.
Since spring there have been hulls past the head running dark. Write that down somewhere.
tg_watchman: Height of water on the hour, all day, all night, and I signal the pilots.
Ninety-six hours of the same number on my slate. That is not a tide.
I sent word to the Institute and to the Foundation. The Foundation came first.
tg_listener_a: I lost a brother off the bar eleven years ago and nobody offered me anything but sorry.
That man is offering something else. I am going to stand here and listen to it.
tg_listener_b: He is not asking for money and he is not asking for a vote.
In my experience that means he already has whatever he came for.
...I am still here, though. Look at me. Still here.
tg_listener_c: Two hundred and six boats. He says that number every time and it is a true number.
You can check it. People have checked it. That is the trouble with him.

_note: LYRA: her standing lines said "I have asked my father four questions this week", which tells the player in Act 2 whose daughter she is. CANON puts that in Act 4 and the Stage 2 brief forbids it here, so the same lines are kept with the relationship taken out -- the four true answers are the good part and they still land. Her one scripted scene is tg_lyra in data/events/common.json and it runs once, after which these take over. TARIN: the ledger in src/systems/tarin.ts publishes tarin_at_<beat> as a flag, and these variants are how the town talks about him between the times he is on screen. They are copies of the shared voices in data/dialogue/common.json (tarin_word_street, _hall, _clinic, _shop) because nothing on any map points an NPC at those ids yet -- if you would rather have the shared ones, set an NPC script to tarin_word_street and delete the copy here. First match wins, so they sit at the top and the ungated line still ends every list.
